from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Cramer's formula is x equals ratio of determinants.",
            "Area of Ax over Area of A.",
            "Linear scaling isolates our scalar weights.",
            "Calculations confirm the geometric intuition.",
            "System solutions emerge from area ratios."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Putting it Together: The Visual Formula", lecture_lines)

        # Assets
        formula = MathTex(r"x = \frac{\det(A_x)}{\det(A)}", font_size=48)
        area_a = Square(side_length=1.5, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        area_ax = Square(side_length=3.0, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture_texts[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B3')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture_texts[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(area_a, 'E2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(area_ax, 'E5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(area_a), Create(area_ax))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture_texts[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        # Visualizing linear scaling: 1.5 * 2 = 3.0
        label_a = Text("Area A", font_size=18).next_to(area_a, DOWN)
        label_ax = Text("Area Ax", font_size=18).next_to(area_ax, DOWN)
        self.play(FadeIn(label_a), FadeIn(label_ax))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture_texts[3].set_color("#00FFFF")
        ratio = MathTex(r"\frac{3.0}{1.5} = 2", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(ratio, 'C3')
        self.play(Write(ratio))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture_texts[4].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(Indicate(formula))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Intuition Check", [
            "Cramer's Rule turns algebra into geometry.", 
            "Problem solving becomes comparing areas.", 
            "It fails when vectors are collinear."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Review key geometric concepts.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        v1 = Vector([1, 1.5], color=BLUE)
        v2 = Vector([2, 0.5], color=RED)
        
        # Draw axes
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 3], y_range=[-1, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.4)
        self.place_at_grid(axes, "C2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Initial parallelogram
        poly = Polygon([0,0,0], [1,1.5,0], [3,2,0], [2,0.5,0], color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(poly, "C2", scale_factor=0.4)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(v1), Create(v2), Create(poly))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Reiterate the area-based intuition.
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        area_label = Text("Area Comparison", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(area_label, "A2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(area_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show the final formula summary.
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # Collapse vectors
        v2_new = Vector([0.5, 0.75], color=RED)
        
        self.play(
            v2.animate.put_start_and_end_on(ORIGIN, [0.5, 0.75, 0]),
            poly.animate.become(Line([0,0,0], [1,1.5,0], color=YELLOW)),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        fail_label = Text("Determinant = 0", font_size=20, color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(fail_label, "E4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(fail_label))
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Determinants as Area
sections.content: Briefly define the determinant of a 2x2 matrix as the 'signed area' of a parallelogram formed by the column vectors (a, b) and (c, d). Visualize this as a transformation of the unit square.
sections.example: Visualize the vector pair [2, 0] and [0, 2] creating a square with area 4. The determinant is 4.

sections.title: Framing the System as Column Vectors
sections.content: Introduce the system Ax = b as a linear combination of columns: x(col1) + y(col2) = b. Explain that we are looking for the 'weights' x and y that scale the columns to reach the target point b.
sections.example: A delivery drone (target b) is powered by two propellers with thrust vectors v1 and v2. We need to find the power settings x and y to reach the target.

sections.title: Geometric Substitution (The 'Area-Ratio' Logic)
sections.content: Explain Cramer's Rule geometrically: Replacing a column vector with b creates a new parallelogram. The ratio of the area of this new parallelogram to the original determines the scalar needed to reach the target.
sections.example: Show an animation where replacing the 'x-axis' vector with the target vector 'b' creates a new shape. The ratio of its area to the original area gives the x-coordinate.

sections.title: Putting it Together: The Visual Formula
sections.content: Formalize the rule: x = Det(A_x) / Det(A). Explain that because areas scale linearly, the ratio of areas perfectly isolates the scalar we are searching for.
sections.example: Calculate x for a system: 2x + 1y = 5, 1x + 2y = 4. Use the visual area boxes to show how the division of the 'new' parallelogram area by the 'original' area results in x=2, y=1.

sections.title: Summary & Intuition Check
sections.content: Conclude by highlighting why this is powerful: It turns a 'searching for unknowns' problem into an 'area comparison' problem. Note the limitation: This only works when the determinant is non-zero (i.e., vectors aren't collinear).
sections.example: An animation of two vectors collapsing into a single line (determinant 0) to show why Cramer's rule fails when the 'parallelogram' has no area.
